children: Tesla is working on a version of its top-selling Model Y SUV that will have no steering wheel or pedals, Chief Executive Elon Musk said Wednesday.
Musk, speaking at the New York Times DealBook Summit, said Tesla wants to offer a fully autonomous vehicle for ride-hailing that could fit a "whole family in the car."
"So what we plan to do is have an autonomous version of Model Y that wouldn't have steering wheels and pedals, and would be good for transporting groups of six or seven people," he said.

An autonomous Model Y could ferry more passengers than the Cybercab, which seats two. That vehicle is used in Tesla's Robotaxi service, but the company recently opened orders for private sale as well.

The Model Y is now Tesla's best-selling EV. Musk said Wednesday that the newest variant-the larger Model YL- has become the most popular version. "I think we probably need to change all of the Model Y production to the YL because it's what most people seem to want," he said.
This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
